MUAP 2101.description: Applied music encompasses the areas of instrumental and vocal performance. It is offered in the form of private lessons for music majors and minors.
MUAP 2101.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major or minor.
MUAP 2101.title: Applied Lessons

MUAP 2102.description: Applied music encompasses the areas of instrumental and vocal performance. It is offered in the form of private lessons for music majors and minors.
MUAP 2102.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major or minor.
MUAP 2102.title: Applied Lessons

MUAP 3096.description: Junior Recital is taken concurrently with applied lessons during the third year of applied studies.
MUAP 3096.title: Junior Recital (Music Performance)

MUAP 3100.description: Applied music encompasses the areas of instrumental and vocal performance. It is offered in the form of private lessons for music majors and minors.
MUAP 3100.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music minor.
MUAP 3100.title: Applied Lessons

MUAP 3101.description: Applied music encompasses the areas of instrumental and vocal performance. It is offered in the form of private lessons for music majors and minors.
MUAP 3101.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major and have taken and passed four semesters of MUAP 2101.
MUAP 3101.title: Applied Lessons

MUAP 3102.description: Applied music encompasses the areas of instrumental and vocal performance. It is offered in the form of private lessons for music majors and minors.
MUAP 3102.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUAP 3102.title: Applied Lessons

MUAP 4000.description: This course combines study with practical application in masterclass settings. Students explore performance traditions from early music to contemporary practice through research, listening, and score study, while also presenting prepared repertoire in class.
MUAP 4000.title: Performance Practice & Criticism

MUAP 4095.description: Senior Recital is taken concurrently with applied lessons during the final on-campus semester.
MUAP 4095.title: Senior Recital (Music Education)

MUAP 4096.description: Senior Recital is taken concurrently with applied lessons during the final on-campus semester.
MUAP 4096.title: Senior Recital (Music Performance)

MUED 3005.description: In this course, students will learn to utilize various technology programs for the music classroom to assist with course development, ensemble performance, and overall student achievement.
MUED 3005.prereqText: EDUC 2110 and admission into Teacher Education Program
MUED 3005.title: Music Education Technology

MUED 3303.description: The development of specific teaching skills, techniques and materials to support the role of band director and instrumental music teacher. The course prepares prospective instrumental track music specialists for all aspects of the role including curriculum design, rehearsal procedures, methodologies and the study of appropriate band literature. Field component, peer teaching and laboratory conducting are required.
MUED 3303.prereqText: MUTC 3200 ,EDUC 2110 , and admission to the Teacher Education program.
MUED 3303.title: Instrumental Methods, Materials and Curriculum

MUED 3305.description: This course will examine musical literature appropriate for P-12 music classrooms and assist in developing teaching strategies appropriate to a wide range of skill levels. In addition, students will learn to utilize various technology programs in the classroom to assist with course development, ensemble performance, and overall student achievement.
MUED 3305.prereqText: MUTC 3200, EDUC 2110, and admission to the Teacher Education program.
MUED 3305.title: Educational Literature and Technology

MUED 3308.description: Focus on characteristics and abilities of individuals with disabilities and the effect upon musical learning and performance. Students will develop materials and teaching strategies in music appropriate to students with special needs. Content includes current legal, educational, and therapeutic issues as they relate to the teaching of music. This course requires field experiences.
MUED 3308.prereqText: MUTC 3200; admission to the Teacher Education program.
MUED 3308.title: Music Education for Exceptional Students

MUED 3314.description: A survey of large and small choral works from the Renaissance to the present with emphasis on practical performing editions and special attention to contemporary literature.
MUED 3314.title: Choral Literature

MUED 3334.description: An exploration of the interaction of historical, social, and philosophical forces and the development of music education, and the justification of a music education program in schools. Issues of career opportunities in music education are included. This course is required for all music education majors.
MUED 3334.title: Foundations of Music Education

MUED 3340.description: A course designed for preparing elementary school educators to integrate meaningful musical experiences into the classroom. Prospective elementary classroom educators will develop basic concepts, skills, methods of instruction, and teaching competencies in the specific areas of music.
MUED 3340.prereqText: Admission to the Teacher Education program.
MUED 3340.title: Music for Early and Middle Grades

MUED 3351.description: This course provides basic teaching and playing competencies on violin, viola, cello and bass. Students learn technical skills on the instrument and a variety of pedagogical strategies to be used while teaching in a group or individual setting. Students gain the ability to correctly sequence teaching episodes and diagnose and correct common problems in upper-level string playing.
MUED 3351.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3351.title: String Techniques

MUED 3352.description: This course provides basic teaching and playing competencies on cello and/or double bass. Students learn technical skills on the instrument and a variety of pedagogical strategies to be used while teaching in a group or individual setting. Students gain the ability to correctly sequence teaching episodes and will be able to diagnose and correct common problems in lower string playing.
MUED 3352.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3352.title: String Techniques Class II

MUED 3353.description: Guitar Techniques provides for basic teaching and playing competencies on guitar as well as an overview of teaching methodologies for individual and class guitar instruction.
MUED 3353.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3353.title: Guitar Techniques Class

MUED 3355.description: Voice Techniques Class provides for basic teaching competency and basic vocal technique in the area of voice.
MUED 3355.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major
MUED 3355.title: Voice Techniques Class

MUED 3357.description: Percussion Techniques Class provides for basic teaching competency in the area of percussion instruments.
MUED 3357.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3357.title: Percussion Techniques Class

MUED 3360.description: Instrument Techniques are required for all music education majors. They are taken by advisement and provide for the necessary competencies in each of the music education track specializations.
MUED 3360.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3360.title: (Name of Instrument) Techniques

MUED 3361.description: Brass Techniques provides basic teaching and playing competency on trumpet, horn, trombone, euphonium, and tuba.
MUED 3361.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3361.title: Brass Techniques

MUED 3362.description: Instrument techniques are required for all music education majors. They are taken by advisement according to concentration. Brass Techniques Class II provides for basic teaching and playing competency on trombone, euphonium and tuba.
MUED 3362.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3362.title: Brass Techniques Class II

MUED 3363.description: Advanced Techniques in Brass Instrumental pedagogy and performance competency.
MUED 3363.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major and have the permission of the instructor.
MUED 3363.title: Brass Techniques Class III

MUED 3364.description: Instrument Techniques are required for all music education majors. They are taken by advisement according to concentration. Woodwind Techniques Class provides for basic teaching and playing competency on flute, clarinet, saxophone, oboe, and bassoon.
MUED 3364.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major
MUED 3364.title: Woodwind Techniques

MUED 3365.description: Woodwind Techniques I provides for basic teaching and playing competency on clarinet and saxophone.
MUED 3365.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3365.title: Woodwind Techniques Class I

MUED 3366.description: Woodwind Techniques Class II provides for basic teaching and playing competency on bassoon, flute, and oboe.
MUED 3366.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3366.title: Woodwind Techniques Class II

MUED 3367.description: Advanced Techniques in Woodwind instrumental pedagogy and performance competency.
MUED 3367.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major and have the permission of the instructor.
MUED 3367.title: Woodwind Techniques Class III

MUED 3370.description: This course provides a practicum in budgeting, organizing, planning, rehearsing, and performing for high school marching bands. Students will utilize drill writing software to facilitate the creation of formations, transitions, and overall design of marching band shows.
MUED 3370.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3370.title: Marching Band Techniques

MUED 3371.description: Brass/Woodwind/Percussion Techniques provides for basic teaching and playing competency, including pedagogical principles designed for Choral, Elementary, Guitar, and Piano concentrations.
MUED 3371.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3371.title: Brass/Woodwind/Percussion Techniques

MUED 3372.description: Instrument Techniques are required by all music education majors. They are taken by advisement according to track and concentration. Strings/Guitar Techniques provides a split-semester overview, including pedagogical principals designed for Choral, General, and Piano Concentration (not Instrumental, Guitar or String.)
MUED 3372.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUED 3372.title: Strings/Guitar Techniques

MUED 3396.description: A supervised work experience program for a minimum of two academic semesters at a site in business, industry or government. For sophomore-, junior-, or senior-level students who wish to obtain successive on the job experience in conjunction with their academic training.
MUED 3396.prereqText: Approval of the coordinator of cooperative education/internship (Career Services).
MUED 3396.title: Cooperative Study

MUED 3398.description: Full-time teaching experience in a work setting, supervised by music education faculty. Student must comply with requirements indicated by the Center for Education Placements and Partnerships of the Bagwell College of Education. The student attends regularly scheduled team-taught music education seminars.
MUED 3398.prereqText: Previous baccalaureate degree, acceptance into the Teacher Education program, and approval of music education program coordinator.
MUED 3398.title: Internship

MUED 3402.description: This course will examine musical literature appropriate for P-12 vocal music classrooms and assist in developing teaching strategies appropriate to a wide range of skill levels.
MUED 3402.prereqText: MUTC 3200 and admission to the Teacher Education Program
MUED 3402.title: Educational Literature in the Choral Classroom

MUED 3403.description: This course will examine musical literature appropriate for P-12 band classrooms and assist in developing teaching strategies appropriate to a wide range of skill levels.
MUED 3403.prereqText: MUTC 3200 and admission to the Teacher Education Program
MUED 3403.title: Educational Literature in the Band Classroom

MUED 3404.description: This course will examine musical literature appropriate for P-12 orchestra classrooms and assist in developing teaching strategies appropriate to a wide range of skill levels.
MUED 3404.prereqText: MUTC 3200 and admission to the Teacher Education Program
MUED 3404.title: Educational Literature in the Orchestra Classroom

MUED 4000.description: Students will gain advanced skills in diagnosing and correcting pedagogical issues appropriate for secondary music students. Students will learn to utilize appropriate technology and skills to arrange music for developmental students.
MUED 4000.prereqText: Acceptance into the Teacher Education program.
MUED 4000.title: Advanced Pedagogy and Arranging

MUED 4301.description: The development of specific teaching skills, techniques, and materials to support the role of the elementary/general music teacher. The course prepares pre-service teachers for all aspects of the role including curriculum design and the incorporation of a wide variety of methodologies into classroom instruction. Field component and peer teaching required. This course is a requirement for all music education majors.
MUED 4301.prereqText: MUTC 3200 and admission to the Teacher Education Program.
MUED 4301.title: Elementary Methods, Materials, and Curriculum

MUED 4302.description: The development of specific teaching skills, techniques and materials to support the role of the vocal and elementary music teacher. The course prepares prospective choral and elementary music specialists for all aspects of the role including curriculum design, classroom environment and management, rehearsal procedures, methodologies, and the study of appropriate literature. Field component, peer teaching, and laboratory conducting are required.
MUED 4302.prereqText: MUSI 3331, MUSI 4433, and admission to the Teacher Education Program.
MUED 4302.title: Choral Methods, Materials, and Curriculum

MUED 4303.description: The development of specific teaching skills, techniques, and materials to support the role of the band teacher. The course prepares prospective band music specialists for all aspects of the role including curriculum design, classroom environment and management, rehearsal procedures, methodologies, and the study of appropriate literature. Field component, peer teaching, and laboratory conducting are required. Teacher education coursework involving field and clinical experiences require verification of liability insurance and a current GaPSC Pre-Service Certificate issued through enrollment in a KSU program.
MUED 4303.prereqText: MUSI 3332 and admission to the Teacher Education Program
MUED 4303.title: Band Methods, Materials, and Curriculum

MUED 4304.description: The development of specific teaching skills, techniques, and materials to support the role of the orchestra instrumental music teacher. The course prepares prospective instrumental music specialists for all aspects of the role including curriculum design, classroom environment and management, rehearsal procedures, methodologies, and the study of appropriate literature. Field component, peer teaching, and laboratory conducting are required. Teacher education coursework involving field and clinical experiences require verification of liability insurance and a current GaPSC Pre-Service Certificate issued through enrollment in a KSU program.
MUED 4304.prereqText: MUSI 3332 and admission to the Teacher Education Program
MUED 4304.title: Orchestra Methods, Materials, and Curriculum

MUED 4305.description: This is an experiential course with a focus on either Instrumental or Choral Ensemble Literature selection and rehearsal techniques appropriate for beginning and intermediate level ensembles. Students will participate through performance on primary and secondary instruments or by singing various choral parts as well as conducting and rehearsing.
MUED 4305.title: Lab Ensemble (Choral)

MUED 4306.description: This is an experiential course with a focus on lesson planning, literature selection, conducting, and rehearsal techniques for choral and elementary music education students. First-year instrumental music education majors will serve as members of the ensemble as part of their “Voice Techniques” requirement. The ensemble will be student conducted.
MUED 4306.title: Lab Ensemble (Band/Orchestra)

MUED 4400.description: Selected topics of an advanced nature, which may include original research topics.
MUED 4400.prereqText: Approval of the instructor, major area committee, and director of the School of Music prior to registration.
MUED 4400.title: Directed Study

MUED 4470.description: Full-time teaching experience in music education with a designated school district, under the supervision of a cooperating teacher in the field, and a university supervisor. The student must have approval from the School of Music and the Center for Education Placements and Partnerships. The student attends a regularly scheduled team-taught music education seminar.
MUED 4470.prereqText: Admission to Student Teaching and successful completion of senior recital.
MUED 4470.title: Student Teaching/Seminar

MUED 4490.description: Selected special topics in music education, which are consistent with research, curriculum, and/or creative practices.
MUED 4490.prereqText: Approval of instructor and Director of School of Music prior to registration.
MUED 4490.title: Special Topics in Music Education

MUED 4650.description: This course is the first semester of an intensive and extensive co-teaching yearlong clinical experience in music education. Under the guidance of a collaborating teacher and university supervisor and working in multiple environments that include students with exceptionalities and English learners, candidates practice professional competencies that impact student achievement. This experience includes regularly scheduled professional seminars.
MUED 4650.prereqText: Admission to Music Education Admission to Teacher Education Admission to Yearlong Clinical Experience Issued Pre-service Certificate
MUED 4650.title: Yearlong Clinical Experience I

MUED 4660.description: This course is the second semester of an intensive and extensive co-teaching yearlong clinical experience in music education. Under the guidance of a collaborating teacher and university supervisor and working in multiple environments that include students with exceptionalities and English learners, candidates practice professional competencies that impact student achievement. This experience includes regularly scheduled professional seminars.
MUED 4660.prereqText: MUED 4650, Educator Ethics Assessment 360 Eligibility, and GACE Eligibility
MUED 4660.title: Yearlong Clinical Experience II

MUED 4990.description: This graduating senior capstone course focuses on the development of a professional music educator portfolio and other supporting materials. Career and graduate school research are course components. Topics address current issues relative to the emerging music education professional.
MUED 4990.title: Senior Seminar and Portfolio

MUEN 3200.description: The Gospel Choir is open to all students campus-wide. No audition is required to participate in this ensemble. The Gospel Choir performs twice each semester. Non-music majors are highly encouraged to enroll in this ensemble.
MUEN 3200.title: Gospel Choir

MUEN 3201.description: The KSU Parliament is open to all students campus-wide. No audition is required to participate in this ensemble. The KSU Parliament performs twice each semester on collegiate level literature. Non-music majors are highly encouraged to enroll in this ensemble.
MUEN 3201.title: KSU Parliament

MUEN 3202.description: The KSU Bella Voce is open to all students campus-wide. No audition is required to participate in this ensemble. The Bella Voce performs twice each semester on collegiate level literature. Non-music majors are highly encouraged to enroll in this ensemble.
MUEN 3202.title: Bella Voce

MUEN 3210.description: This course is designed to introduce classical ensemble playing to guitarists. The weekly class sessions and performances will help the student develop skills in sight reading, classical guitar styles, and ensemble playing.
MUEN 3210.title: Classical Guitar Ensemble

MUEN 3211.description: This course is designed to introduce jazz ensemble playing to guitarists. The weekly class sessions and performances will help the student develop skills in the following areas: Sight Reading, jazz styles, chord comping, and ensemble playing.
MUEN 3211.title: Jazz Guitar Ensemble

MUEN 3212.description: This course introduces jazz improvisation to students for instrumental performance. Students will perform jazz standards from the Real Book and other sources while applying concepts and patterns studied in class.
MUEN 3212.title: Jazz Combo

MUEN 3220.description: The Percussion Ensemble provides students with the opportunity to study, rehearse, and perform literature for group percussion.
MUEN 3220.title: Percussion Ensemble

MUEN 3221.description: The String Ensemble will allow students to improve ensemble-playing skills in a chamber setting on like stringed instruments. Students will rehearse standard ensemble pieces as well as new compositions and arrangements.
MUEN 3221.title: String Ensemble

MUEN 3222.description: The KSU Woodwind Ensemble provides students rehearsal and performance experience in chamber music settings. Students will experience literature in both classical and jazz idioms.
MUEN 3222.title: Woodwind Ensemble

MUEN 3223.description: The Brass Ensemble is designed to improve ensemble playing in a chamber setting. Brass ensemble members will work on standards ensemble pieces as well as new compositions and arrangements.
MUEN 3223.title: Brass Ensemble

MUEN 3224.description: The Piano Ensemble provides students with the opportunity to perform piano works written for four or more hands in a variety of genres and styles.
MUEN 3224.title: Piano Ensemble

MUEN 3225.description: The Mixed Chamber Ensemble allows students to learn literature in a small group setting with the assistance of faculty coaches. The Mixed Chamber Ensemble focuses on intonation, blend, stylistic awareness, ensemble precision, and knowledge of repertoire.
MUEN 3225.title: Mixed Chamber

MUEN 3341.description: The University Band is a wind band that performs collegiate repertoire twice each semester. Non-music major wind and percussionists are strongly encouraged to enroll in this ensemble. No audition is required for the University Band.
MUEN 3341.title: University Band

MUEN 3342.description: This course develops the instrumental and visual performance skills of students within the college marching band setting. Objectives are to combine high-level musical/visual performance with uniform marching style to create entertaining shows for football games. This course is open to all students in all majors. Auditions are required for participation and occur the week before fall classes begin. This course is offered every fall semester; max 300 members.
MUEN 3342.prereqText: Audition required and prior high school or college instrumental or colorguard experience required.
MUEN 3342.title: Marching Band

MUEN 3343.description: This course may be repeated for upper-division credit. The School of Music offers two large Jazz Ensembles that perform both on- and off-campus in concert. The ensembles perform a variety of styles within the jazz idiom including traditional swing, bop, Latin, Afro-Cuban, and funk.
MUEN 3343.prereqText: Audition and permission of the instructor.
MUEN 3343.title: Jazz Ensemble

MUEN 3344.description: May be repeated for upper-division credit. Study, rehearsal, and concert performance of literature for orchestra. No audition is required and non-music majors with previous orchestral experience are encouraged to play in the group.
MUEN 3344.prereqText: Membership is open to all students with previous experience playing an instrument.
MUEN 3344.title: University Philharmonic Orchestra

MUEN 3345.description: This course offers music majors, minors, and non-music majors the opportunity to study, rehearse, and perform literature for the wind band medium. This course may be repeated for upper-division credit or zero credit. Membership in the Wind Symphony is by audition only.
MUEN 3345.title: Wind Symphony

MUEN 3346.description: May be repeated for upper-division credit. Study, rehearsal and performance of choral literature. Membership in Chamber Singers is by audition only.
MUEN 3346.title: Chamber Singers

MUEN 3347.description: May be repeated for upper-division credit. Study, rehearsal and concert performance of literature for wind ensemble. Membership in the Wind Ensemble is by audition only.
MUEN 3347.title: Wind Ensemble

MUEN 3348.description: May be repeated for upper-division credit. Study, rehearsal and concert performance of literature for orchestra.
MUEN 3348.title: Symphony Orchestra

MUEN 3349.description: May be repeated for upper-division credit. Study, rehearsal and concert performance of literature for choir.
MUEN 3349.title: Chorale

MUEN 3352.description: This course provides students with comprehensive training in the performance and production of opera. Through rehearsal and staged performance, students develop skills in vocal technique, acting, stage movement, and ensemble collaboration. Emphasis is placed on musical accuracy, dramatic interpretation, and professional performance practices. Repertoire includes selections from standard operatic literature as well as scenes from works spanning diverse styles and periods. Open to qualified singers by audition, Opera Theater culminates in public performances that integrate the elements of music, theater, and stagecraft.
MUEN 3352.title: Opera Theater

MUSC 1100.description: Introduction to Music History and Literature.
MUSC 1100.title: Music Appreciation

MUSI 1107.description: This course examines the role of music in society through a study of musical works within their cultural and historical contexts. Course assignments develop skills in critical analysis and global perspectives as well as an understanding of the creative process. Required attendance at live performances provides the experiential component so crucial to the understanding and enjoyment of music. (Most events require paid admission.)
MUSI 1107.title: Music in Society

MUSI 1110.description: Introduction to music of the world’s cultures.
MUSI 1110.title: Introduction to World Music

MUSI 1141.description: The University Band is a wind band that performs collegiate repertoire twice each semester. Non-music major wind and percussionists are strongly encouraged to enroll in this ensemble. No audition is required for the University Band.
MUSI 1141.title: University Band

MUSI 1142.description: This course develops the instrumental and visual performance skills of students within the college marching band setting. Objectives are to combine high-level musical/visual performance with uniform marching style to create entertaining shows suitable for football games. This course is open to students in all majors. Auditions are required for participation and occur the week before fall classes begin. This course is offered every fall semester; max. 300 members.
MUSI 1142.prereqText: Audition required and prior high school or college instrumental or colorguard experience required.
MUSI 1142.title: Marching Band

MUSI 1143.description: This course may be repeated for lower-division credit. The School of Music offers two large Jazz Ensembles that perform both on- and off-campus in concert. The ensembles perform a variety of styles within the jazz idiom including traditional swing, bop, Latin, Afro-Cuban, and funk.
MUSI 1143.prereqText: Audition and permission of the instructor.
MUSI 1143.title: Jazz Ensemble

MUSI 1144.description: May be repeated for lower-division credit. Study, rehearsal, and concert performance of literature for orchestra. No audition is required and non-music majors with previous orchestral experience are encouraged to play in the group.
MUSI 1144.prereqText: Membership is open to all students with previous experience playing an instrument.
MUSI 1144.title: University Philharmonic Orchestra

MUSI 1145.description: This course offers music majors, minors, and non-music majors the opportunity to study, rehearse, and perform literature for the wind band medium. This course may be repeated for lower-division credit. Membership in the Wind Symphony is by audition only.
MUSI 1145.title: Wind Symphony

MUSI 1146.description: May be repeated for lower-division credit. Study, rehearsal, and concert performance of choral literature. Membership in Chamber Singers is by audition only.
MUSI 1146.title: Chamber Singers

MUSI 1147.description: May be repeated for lower-division credit. Study, rehearsal and concert performance of literature for wind ensemble. Membership in Wind Ensemble is by audition only.
MUSI 1147.title: Wind Ensemble

MUSI 1148.description: May be repeated for lower-division credit. Study, rehearsal and concert performance of literature for orchestra. Membership in the Orchestra is by audition only.
MUSI 1148.title: Symphony Orchestra

MUSI 1149.description: May be repeated for lower-division credit. Study, rehearsal and concert performance of literature for choir.
MUSI 1149.title: Chorale

MUSI 1165.description: The purpose of class piano instruction is to equip non-piano majors with the keyboard proficiencies needed to be reasonably fluent in basic technical and reading skills for practical use as a professional musician.
MUSI 1165.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major; placement determined by proficiency test.
MUSI 1165.title: Class Piano I

MUSI 3000.description: The development of practical experience with current computer applications and current technology specifically associated with music instruction and music performance. The course exposes students to current capabilities of technology as they relate to composition, instrumentation, performance and teaching.
MUSI 3000.title: Technology in Music

MUSI 3010.description: This course is an introduction to the principles of Alexander Technique and its application to performance in music, theater, or dance. Alexander Technique is a way of working to improve ease of movement, develop greater poise and confidence in performance of various activities, and is helpful in preventing or recovering from injury.
MUSI 3010.prereqText: Admitted major in the College of the Arts
MUSI 3010.title: Alexander Technique for Performers

MUSI 3167.description: This course will allow students to continue their piano training and apply specific accompanying and instructional techniques to choral literature for the classroom.
MUSI 3167.title: Class Piano V

MUSI 3302.description: Vocal literature, vocal techniques, and performance for the musical theater. This course will survey the musical repertory of standard major musical theater works. Students will prepare and perform songs, duets and group numbers from several musicals.
MUSI 3302.prereqText: ENGL 1101 and permission of the instructor.
MUSI 3302.title: Vocal Literature: Musical Theater

MUSI 3315.description: Solo vocal literature from 1600 to the present.
MUSI 3315.title: Vocal Literature

MUSI 3318.description: Orchestral literature from Classical Era to present including symphony, concerto, concert overture, incidental music, program symphony, and tone poem. Emphasis on standard literature.
MUSI 3318.title: Introduction to Symphonic Music

MUSI 3331.description: Fundamental elements of conducting including baton technique, score reading, cueing, expression, interpretation and rehearsal skills with an emphasis on applying these techniques in practical conducting experiences involving vocal and instrumental ensembles.
MUSI 3331.title: Choral Conducting

MUSI 3332.description: Fundamental elements of conducting including baton technique, score reading, cueing, expression, interpretation and rehearsal skills with an emphasis on applying these techniques in practical conducting experiences involving vocal and instrumental ensembles.
MUSI 3332.title: Instrumental Conducting

MUSI 3333.description: May be repeated for upper-division credit. For music majors. The practical application of accompaniment techniques.
MUSI 3333.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major; and permission of the instructor.
MUSI 3333.title: Accompanying

MUSI 3334.description: Designed for the vocal music major. The study of the pronunciation, enunciation, and expression of the Italian and English language in singing.
MUSI 3334.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUSI 3334.title: Italian and English Diction

MUSI 3335.description: Designed for the vocal music majors. An applied performance laboratory for the study of the pronunciation, enunciation, and expression of the German and French language in singing.
MUSI 3335.title: German and French Diction

MUSI 3336.description: This course will focus on applying the International Phonetic Alphabet to the transliteration of French, German, Italian, and English languages.
MUSI 3336.prereqText: Must be a fully-admitted music major.
MUSI 3336.title: Diction for Singers

MUSI 3350.description: Advanced elements of conducting including baton technique, score reading, cueing, expression, interpretation and rehearsal skills with an emphasis on applying these techniques through choral literature in practical conducting experiences involving choral ensembles. Required laboratory component.
MUSI 3350.title: Advanced Choral Conducting/Literature

MUSI 3351.description: Advanced elements of conducting including baton technique, score reading, cueing, expression, interpretation and rehearsal skills with an emphasis on applying these techniques through band and orchestra literature in practical conducting experiences involving instrumental ensembles. Required laboratory component.
MUSI 3351.title: Advanced Instrumental Conducting/Literature

MUSI 3353.description: An introduction to jazz improvisation for any instrument and application of jazz improvisation techniques to jazz repertoire including modal compositions, blues, minor blues, and compositions with major cadences.
MUSI 3353.title: Jazz Improvisation I

MUSI 3354.description: A continuing methodology designed to improve jazz improvisation, for any instrument and application in jazz, that focuses on rhythm changes form, altered dominants, bebop concepts, and unconventional harmonies.
MUSI 3354.title: Jazz Improvisation II

MUSI 3355.description: A continuing methodology designed to improve jazz improvisation, for any instrument and application in jazz, that focuses on melodic minor derivations, cycling altered dominants, pentatonic concepts, and non-traditional harmonies.
MUSI 3355.title: Jazz Improvisation III

MUSI 3360.description: An introduction to jazz piano skills for the non-pianist including interpreting chord symbols and sophisticated harmonies, learning functional voicings, and performance competency.
MUSI 3360.title: Jazz Piano

MUSI 3361.description: The purpose of this course is to train jazz vocalists to perform basic- to intermediate-level accompaniment on the piano while singing.
MUSI 3361.title: Piano Accompaniment for Jazz Vocalists

MUSI 3367.description: Vocal proficiency for music majors and non-majors. Emphasis on tone production, diction, performing skills and the physiology of the voice.
MUSI 3367.prereqText: All developmental studies courses if required. Non-music majors require permission of the instructor.
MUSI 3367.title: Vocal Skills I

MUSI 3390.description: Students will work on a series of projects to understand aspects of what is required to have a successful career in the music industry in the 21st century and build the skills beyond musicianship that will aid in attaining musical goals.
MUSI 3390.prereqText: Acceptance into the Music Entertainment and Business program or completion of MUTC 3200
MUSI 3390.title: Music Entrepreneurship

MUSI 3396.description: A supervised work experience program for a minimum of two academic semesters at a site in business, industry or government. For sophomore-, junior, or senior level students who wish to obtain successive on the job experience in conjunction with their academic training.
MUSI 3396.prereqText: Approval of the coordinator of cooperative education/internship (Career Services).
MUSI 3396.title: Cooperative Study

MUSI 3398.description: A supervised, credit earning work experience of one academic semester with a previously approved business firm, private agency or government agency.
MUSI 3398.title: Internship

MUSI 4400.description: Selected topics of an advanced nature, which may include original research projects.
MUSI 4400.prereqText: Approval of the instructor, major area committee and department chair prior to registration.
MUSI 4400.title: Directed Study

MUSI 4410.description: Music literature from Impressionism to the present.
MUSI 4410.title: Contemporary Music Literature

MUSI 4413.description: Keyboard literature from 1600 to the present.
MUSI 4413.prereqText: MUTC 2200 and permission of the instructor
MUSI 4413.title: Piano Literature I

MUSI 4414.description: Continuation of keyboard literature from 1600 to the present.
MUSI 4414.prereqText: MUSI 4413 or permission of the instructor.
MUSI 4414.title: Piano Literature II

MUSI 4423.description: This course offers an introduction to musicology including its origins, development and methodologies. Students will develop skills necessary for critical enquiry in music through engagement with theories of historiography, aesthetics, and performance practice, as well as critical assessment of current issues in the field.
MUSI 4423.title: Current Directions in Musicology

MUSI 4430.description: Beginning-, elementary, and intermediate level teaching materials and methods for piano.
MUSI 4430.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major.
MUSI 4430.title: Piano Pedagogy I

MUSI 4431.description: Continuation of beginning-, elementary-, and intermediate-level teaching materials and methods for piano.
MUSI 4431.prereqText: MUSI 4430 and permission of the instructor.
MUSI 4431.title: Piano Pedagogy II

MUSI 4433.description: Pedagogical methods, vocal physiology and literature for training voices from beginning to advanced levels.
MUSI 4433.title: Voice Pedagogy

MUSI 4434.description: Pedagogical methods for voice and vocal ensembles, vocal physiology and literature for training voices from beginning to advanced levels.
MUSI 4434.title: Vocal Pedagogy for Ensemble Singing

MUSI 4435.description: Pedagogical methods, techniques, physiology and literature in the principal performance concentration area.
MUSI 4435.title: (Name of Instrument) Pedagogy and Literature

MUSI 4436.description: This course introduces students to the methodologies and resources of jazz pedagogy. Students will learn appropriate literature for a variety of age levels as well as rehearsal techniques for both the large and small jazz ensemble.
MUSI 4436.title: Jazz Pedagogy

MUSI 4480.description: A research project based on the literature to be presented in the senior recital. Analysis of the literature. Program notes to be drawn from research and analysis.
MUSI 4480.title: Research for Senior Recital

MUSI 4490.description: Selected special topics of interest to faculty and students.
MUSI 4490.prereqText: Approval of the instructor and department chair.
MUSI 4490.title: Special Topics in Music

MUSI 4495.description: A capstone course designed to complete the major by integrating the student’s prior academic, theoretical and applied experiences in music. Students fulfill projects in areas of musical performance, lecture presentations, creative work, scholarly documents, pedagogy or arts advocacy.
MUSI 4495.prereqText: Completion of applied studies and completion of 90 hours of course work and permission of the instructor and capstone committee one semester prior to registration.
MUSI 4495.title: Senior Seminar in Music

MUTC 1020.description: The fundamentals of music theory including music reading, rhythm and pitch orientation, accidentals, key and time signatures, rhythmic organization, intervals, scale formation, triad construction and chord spelling, elementary ear training and sight singing, and an introduction to the keyboard. Open to all university students. May not be counted for credit towards a music degree.
MUTC 1020.title: Fundamentals of Music Theory

MUTC 1120.description: For music majors and minors. A correlated study of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic aspects of music common practice. Development of basic skills in music theory and harmony including practical application through part-writing. Components include composition, improvisation, and practical keyboard applications. Contains a separate keyboard lab to increase proficiency.
MUTC 1120.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major or minor; placement determined by a proficiency test.
MUTC 1120.title: Music Theory I Intensive

MUTC 2100.description: A correlated study of rhythmic, melodic and harmonic aspects of music common practice. Development of basic skills in music theory and harmony including practical application through part-writing. Components include composition, improvisation and practical keyboard applications.
MUTC 2100.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major or minor; placement determined by proficiency test.
MUTC 2100.title: Music Theory I

MUTC 2110.description: Foundation work in sight singing including rhythmic and melodic dictation. Practical application includes some composition and improvisation.
MUTC 2110.prereqText: Must be a fully admitted music major or minor; placement determined by proficiency test.
MUTC 2110.title: Aural Skills I

MUTC 2200.description: A continuation of correlated study of rhythmic, melodic and harmonic aspects of music common practice. Continuation of keyboard harmony is included with application at the keyboard. Components include composition, improvisation and practical keyboard applications.
MUTC 2200.title: Music Theory II

MUTC 2210.description: Continuation of skill development in sight singing including rhythmic and melodic dictation. Practical application includes some composition and improvisation.
MUTC 2210.title: Aural Skills II

MUTC 3007.description: This course provides background, training and experience for the student in the area of scoring for media including film, television and gaming.
MUTC 3007.title: Scoring for Media

MUTC 3100.description: Advanced correlated study of music theory and harmony of common practice including chromatic harmony and 20th century harmonic techniques. Components include composition, improvisation, literature analysis and practical keyboard application.
MUTC 3100.title: Music Theory III

MUTC 3110.description: For music majors. Advanced skill development in ear training and sight singing. Includes rhythmic and melodic dictation. Practical application includes some composition and improvisation.
MUTC 3110.title: Aural Skills III

MUTC 3168.description: This course trains music majors in advanced keyboard harmony to prepare them for graduate-level music programs. Component skills may include the performance of harmonic progressions in all keys, memorized intermediate-level repertoire, score reading, figured bass realization, and improvisation.
MUTC 3168.title: Advanced Keyboard Harmony

MUTC 3200.description: For music majors. Continuation of advanced correlated study of music theory and harmony in common practice including analytical study of 20th century music. Components include composition, improvisation, literature analysis and practical keyboard application.
MUTC 3200.title: Music Theory IV

MUTC 3210.description: Continuation of advanced skill development in ear training and sight singing. Includes rhythmic and melodic dictation. Practical application includes some composition and improvisation.
MUTC 3210.title: Aural Skills IV

MUTC 3313.description: This course introduces students to the language of jazz, including chord nomenclature and spelling, chord/scale relationships, chord function, and reharmonization techniques.
MUTC 3313.title: Jazz Theory

MUTC 3320.description: Techniques of structural analysis of musical compositions in a variety of styles and periods with emphasis on harmony and form. The analysis of contrapuntal form is included.
MUTC 3320.title: Form and Analysis

MUTC 3321.description: Extended training in harmonic dictation, sight singing, aural analysis and rhythm.
MUTC 3321.title: Advanced Ear Training

MUTC 3322.description: This course introduces the language of jazz and its application to jazz performance, improvisation, analysis and composition.
MUTC 3322.title: Jazz Theory and Composition

MUTC 3323.description: A study of jazz arranging techniques for jazz ensembles. Students will arrange works for big band and jazz combos.
MUTC 3323.prereqText: MUTC 3313, or permission of the instructor.
MUTC 3323.title: Jazz Arranging

MUTC 3324.description: A study of the characteristics of orchestral instruments, including scoring principals and techniques. In addition the course includes the arranging of musical works for a variety of large and small vocal and instrumental ensembles.
MUTC 3324.title: Instrumentation/Arranging

MUTC 3325.description: This course will introduce common song forms and compositional techniques in the jazz idiom in addition to analysis of lead sheets and large ensemble scores.
MUTC 3325.prereqText: MUTC 3313 or permission of the instructor
MUTC 3325.title: Jazz Forms and Composition

MUTC 3326.description: Students develop music composition skills by exploring basic techniques necessary for coherent creative expression. By writing original compositions for various instrumentations, students gain skills in the artistic use of pitch, rhythm, melody, timbre and harmony. 20th and 21st century styles and techniques are utilized, and students acquire skill in music improvisation. Students gain competency in the basics of music notation utilizing both calligraphy and composition software.
MUTC 3326.prereqText: MUTC 2200 or (MUTC 2100 with a “B” or higher”) or (MUTC 1120 with a “B” or higher)
MUTC 3326.title: Class Composition I

MUTC 3327.description: Students develop further music composition skill by exploring techniques necessary for coherent creative expression. By writing original compositions for various instrumentations, students gain abilities in the artistic use of pitch, rhythm, melody, timbre and harmony. 20th and 21st century styles and techniques are utilized. Students gain technology competency in the use of composition software and by learning the basics of digital audio and video editing of recorded performances.
MUTC 3327.title: Class Composition II

MUTC 3328.description: For music majors. A seminar on the current music theory and musicology writings on multimedia music. Students will trace the progression of multimedia music from its 19th-Century precedents through current music. Students will analyze correlations between music and other media signifiers and how they generate structure and meaning. Components include research, presentations, and writing.
MUTC 3328.title: Introduction to Musical Multimedia Theory

MUTC 3371.description: Individually tailored instruction is utilized for the development of music composition skills by writing in traditional and contemporary styles in both small and large forms and for a variety of media.
MUTC 3371.prereqText: MUTC 2200, or MUTC 2100, or MUTC 1120 with a “B” or higher
MUTC 3371.title: Composition I

MUTC 3372.description: Individually tailored instruction is utilized for the development of music composition skills by writing in traditional and contemporary styles in both small and large forms and for a variety of media.
MUTC 3372.prereqText: MUTC 3371 and permission of the instructor.
MUTC 3372.title: Composition II

MUTC 4419.description: A study of tonal, common-practice music in the Western art music tradition from the perspective of Schenkerian (reductive) analysis. Activities include investigations of harmony, voice leading, form, and implications for performance. Encourages students to debate the merits of different analyzes of the same work. Culminates in scholarly research by the student that builds upon previous Schenkerian analyzes. A writing-intensive course.
MUTC 4419.title: Introduction to Schenker

MUTC 4420.description: Analysis and principles of writing in the contrapuntal styles of the common practice period to the present.
MUTC 4420.title: Counterpoint

MUTC 4421.description: This course surveys 20th- and 21st-century musical styles and theoretical systems, teaching students how to analyze a variety of works in which Common-Practice Period norms of tonality, rhythm, form, timbre, and texture have been superseded by new developments. Corresponding compositional exercises deepen student understanding of these new approaches. Topics include free atonality, serialism, neoclassicism, minimalism, allusions, chance, and electronic composition. The course prepares students to analyze music, write model compositions, and develop analytical papers.
MUTC 4421.title: Contemporary Analytical and Compositional Techniques

MUTC 4422.description: This course introduces music majors to the field of music theory pedagogy and enables students to teach written theory and aural skills at the undergraduate level. Students team-teach lessons in undergraduate courses in the School of Music and prepare materials for potential graduate school applications.
MUTC 4422.title: Music Theory Pedagogy

MUTC 4471.description: Individually tailored instruction is utilized for the development of music composition skills by writing in traditional and contemporary styles in both small and large forms and for a variety of media.
MUTC 4471.prereqText: MUTC 3327 or MUTC 3372 and permission of the instructor.
MUTC 4471.title: Composition III

MUTC 4472.description: Individually tailored instruction is utilized for the development of music composition skills by writing in traditional and contemporary styles in both small and large forms and for a variety of media.
MUTC 4472.prereqText: MUTC 4471 and permission of the instructor.
MUTC 4472.title: Composition IV

MUTC 4473.description: Individually tailored instruction is utilized for the development of music composition skills by writing in traditional and contemporary styles in both small and large forms and for a variety of media.
MUTC 4473.title: Composition V

MUTC 4474.description: Advanced individually tailored instruction is utilized for the development of music composition skills by writing in traditional and contemporary styles in both small and large forms and for a variety of media.
MUTC 4474.title: Composition VI

MUTC 4496.description: A senior-level research course designed to provide a learning experience that integrates the student’s prior academic, theoretical, research, and applied experiences in music. Students fulfill projects that synthesize and disseminate their work through a lecture, lecture-performance, or scholarly paper.
MUTC 4496.prereqText: Completion of 90 hours of course work and admitted music major.
MUTC 4496.title: Senior Capstone Music Project

MUTC 4497.description: A senior-level composition course designed to provide a learning experience that integrates the student’s prior academic, theoretical, research, and applied experiences in music. Students fulfill projects that synthesize and disseminate their work through a culminating lecture-performance.
MUTC 4497.prereqText: MUTC 4473 and completion of 90 hours of coursework
MUTC 4497.title: Senior Composition Capstone Project

MUTH 1000.description: This course provides an overview of the music therapy field, introducing students to its history, scope of practice, clinical applications, and professional competencies. In this course, students will explore how music therapy integrates musical, psychological, and therapeutic principles to address the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social needs of individuals across diverse populations and settings.
MUTH 1000.title: Introduction to the Profession of Music Therapy

MUTH 2000.description: This course provides an introduction to foundational principles of music therapy practice. Students examine professional ethics and competencies while developing beginning clinical skills through case studies and guided observation. This course provides the foundation for practicum and advanced clinical training in music therapy.
MUTH 2000.title: Clinical Foundations in Music Therapy

MUTH 2100.description: This course introduces theories, principles, and methods of music therapy practice. Students explore the therapeutic relationship, clinical applications of music across populations, and the integration of psychological and physiological concepts into treatment planning. Emphasis is placed on historical and contemporary models of music therapy, ethical standards of practice, and developing observation, assessment, and intervention skills.
MUTH 2100.title: Music Therapy Theory & Application I

MUTH 2500.description: This course develops functional guitar skills essential for the practice of music therapy. Students will learn chord vocabulary, strumming and fingerpicking patterns, transposition, improvisation, and song-leading techniques that support therapeutic goals in clinical settings.
MUTH 2500.title: Guitar Skills for Music Therapists

MUTH 3150.description: This course is a supervised clinical experience introducing students to the application of music therapy in professional settings. Students observe, assist, and begin to facilitate music experiences with diverse populations under the guidance of board-certified music therapists. Emphasis is placed on developing professional skills, including session planning, clinical observation, therapeutic presence, ethical practice, and reflective journaling. Practicum I provides students with a structured opportunity to connect classroom learning with clinical practice, laying the foundation for progressive practicum experiences and professional competency in music therapy.
MUTH 3150.title: Music Therapy Practicum I

MUTH 3250.description: This course provides continued supervised clinical training for students in music therapy, building upon skills developed in Practicum I. Students engage in structured field experiences in healthcare, educational, and/or community settings, applying music therapy methods with increasing independence and clinical responsibility. Emphasis is placed on treatment planning, implementation, observation, documentation, and reflection. Students will further develop therapeutic presence, adaptability, and professional communication skills while working with diverse client populations.
MUTH 3250.title: Music Therapy Practicum II

MUTH 3300.description: This course introduces students to the principles, methods, and applications of research and assessment in music therapy. Students will explore qualitative and quantitative research designs, evidence-based practices, and ethical considerations in clinical work. Emphasis is placed on analyzing scholarly literature and applying research findings to clinical practice. Students will also gain hands-on experience with assessment tools and techniques used to evaluate client needs, track progress, and measure treatment outcomes.
MUTH 3300.title: Music Therapy Research & Assessment

MUTH 3350.description: This course provides music therapy students with expanded clinical experience and increasing responsibility in a supervised setting. Students engage in structured music therapy sessions across diverse populations, with emphasis on session planning, treatment documentation, therapeutic communication, and professional ethics. Building on prior practica, students are expected to demonstrate greater independence in leading interventions, integrating music therapy methods with clinical goals, and applying theoretical knowledge to practice. Regular supervision and reflective assignments guide students in refining their clinical musicianship, interpersonal skills, and professional identity as developing music therapists.
MUTH 3350.title: Music Therapy Practicum III

MUTH 3400.description: This course builds upon the foundations established in Music Therapy Theory & Application I, advancing students’ understanding of clinical techniques, treatment planning, and theoretical models in music therapy. Emphasis is placed on the application of music interventions for diverse populations, including individuals across the lifespan with varying developmental, medical, and psychological needs.
MUTH 3400.title: Music Therapy Theory & Application II

MUTH 3450.description: This advanced practicum provides supervised clinical experience in diverse music therapy settings, emphasizing greater independence, leadership, and professional competence. Students refine their ability to assess client needs, design and implement individualized interventions, and evaluate outcomes using evidence-based practices. The course integrates advanced clinical musicianship with professional documentation, treatment planning, and ethical decision-making. By the fourth practicum, students are expected to demonstrate increased autonomy in leading sessions, collaborate effectively with interdisciplinary teams, and begin developing a personal therapeutic style that reflects best practices in the field. Regular supervision and peer feedback guide the integration of theory, research, and practice, preparing students for the culminating internship and entry into professional music therapy practice.
MUTH 3450.title: Music Therapy Practicum IV

MUTH 3500.description: This course advances students’ understanding of the theoretical foundations and applied practices of music therapy with a focus on clinical decision-making and treatment planning across diverse populations. Students refine skills in assessment, goal development, intervention design, and documentation while integrating current research and evidence-based practices. Emphasis is placed on the therapeutic relationship, clinical improvisation, and ethical considerations in music therapy practice. Through lecture, discussion, and applied experiences, students deepen their capacity to synthesize theory and application in preparation for advanced practicum and clinical work.
MUTH 3500.title: Music Therapy Theory & Application III

MUTH 4150.description: This course is the culminating practicum providing music therapy majors with advanced, supervised clinical training in preparation for internship. Students refine their clinical musicianship, therapeutic presence, and professional competencies through immersive placements in diverse healthcare and community settings. Emphasis is placed on independent treatment planning, implementation, documentation, and evaluation, as well as integration of theoretical knowledge with clinical decision-making. Students are expected to demonstrate entry-level proficiency in applying music therapy methods across populations, collaborating with interdisciplinary teams, and adhering to professional and ethical standards. Successful completion of this practicum confirms readiness for internship and transition into the professional field of music therapy.
MUTH 4150.title: Music Therapy Practicum V

MUTH 4500.description: The culminating clinical experience for music therapy majors, the Music Therapy Internship provides full-time supervised training at an American Music Therapy Association National Roster Internship site or University Affiliate location. The internship experience is designed to strengthen areas of competency and address individual skill needs while fostering professional growth. Students apply advanced skills in assessment, treatment planning, intervention, evaluation, and professional documentation while working with diverse client populations. Completion of the internship fulfills the clinical training requirement necessary to sit for national board certification as a Music Therapist-Board Certified (MT-BC). Once the national certification is achieved, the student qualifies for a music therapy license in the state of Georgia (LPMT).
MUTH 4500.title: Music Therapy Internship

NS 1000.description: Leadership Laboratory is an engaging and interactive professional development course required every semester for Navy and Marine option Midshipmen in the NROTC program.
NS 1000.title: Naval Science Leadership Lab

NS 1321.description: This course is an introduction and orientation class designed to give students a broad overview of the roles of the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps. This course also provides an introduction to the structure, terminology, customs, and uniforms of the Navy and Marine Corps.
NS 1321.title: Introduction to Naval Science

NS 1323.description: This course surveys U.S. Naval history from its European origin to the present with emphasis on major developments and the geographical forces shaping these developments. The course also covers present day concerns on sea power and maritime affairs, including the economic and political issues of maritime commerce, the law of the sea, and the rise and decline of the Soviet Navy.
NS 1323.title: Naval Maritime History

NS 2321.description: This course provides the basis for the development of effective leadership and managerial competence. It stresses learner-centered processes, such as collaboration, experiential exercises, reflective writing, and group discussion over lecture and presentations. Case study discussions are sequenced throughout the course to illustrate the relevance of key concepts presented in preceding class sessions and relate these ideas to the Fleet. Student participation is critical to this course.
NS 2321.title: Naval Leadership and Management

NS 2323.description: This course is Marine navigation which blends both science and art. Students are taught how information from every available source is evaluated and compared. Navigators constantly evaluate a ship’s position, anticipates dangerous situations well before they arise, and always keeps “ahead of the vessel.” The modern navigator must also understand the basic concepts of the many navigation systems used today, evaluate the accuracy of output, and arrive at the best possible navigational decisions.
NS 2323.title: Navigation

NS 3323.description: A historical exploration of warfare practiced by great nations. Selected campaigns are studied with emphasis on leadership, evolution of tactics, weaponry, and principles of war.
NS 3323.title: Evolution of Warfare

NS 3325.description: This course is designed to give students an in-depth understanding of naval weapons, their associated systems, and the integration of these weapon systems into the overall battle plan of the U.S. Navy while also reviewing Navy and Marine Corps platforms and their associated capabilities.
NS 3325.title: Naval Weapon Systems

NS 3326.description: This course is designed to develop and broaden the student’s understanding of basic engineering concepts and principles as applied to naval engineering plants. The course will provide students with an understanding of naval engineering concepts that will be applied first-hand while on summer cruise in preparation for their division officer tours. It is not the intend of this course to cover each area in great detail, but rather to stimulate the interest of students for study and investigation in the future.
NS 3326.title: Naval Systems Engineering

NS 4320.description: This course is an in-depth study of numerous aspects relating to the efficient and professional manner of U.S. Navy ships’ operations.
NS 4320.title: Naval Operations

NS 4322.description: Study of Naval values and ethics to include core values, Navy regulations, and military law. Duties and responsibilities of a junior naval officer.
NS 4322.title: Naval Leadership and Ethics

NS 4333.description: This course analyzes the United States Marine Corps as the overarching case study for the advent of maneuver warfare. This is a history and doctrine-based course. The object is to educate students in the characteristics, requirements, and problems of maneuver warfare. Although this course focuses on maneuver warfare, it is worthwhile to point out that maneuver warfare is merely a subset of warfare in general. While it exhibits certain unique characteristics, it also shares many characteristics with the broader field.
NS 4333.title: Fundamentals of Maneuver Warfare

NURS 3101.description: In this course, students learn foundational concepts of professional nursing practice, including the nursing process, clinical judgment, and ethical practice. They develop skills in therapeutic and interprofessional communication, culturally responsive care, and health promotion across the lifespan. The course emphasizes safety, evidence-based decision-making, coping and resiliency, and professional accountability. Students explore legal responsibilities, including documentation and advance directives, and examine the impact of social determinants of health. Students build competencies essential for delivering safe, ethical, and patient-centered nursing care.
NURS 3101.title: Nursing Care I: Foundations of Nursing Practice

NURS 3102.description: In this course, students apply core nursing concepts, develop essential patient care skills, and cultivate professional and ethical behaviors. Emphasis is placed on clear, therapeutic, and professional communication with patients, families, and interprofessional healthcare teams to ensure safe, person-centered care. Students develop clinical judgment to assess patients, implement evidence-based care, and evaluate outcomes in diverse populations. Experiential learning takes place in the skills lab, simulation lab, and various community settings.
NURS 3102.title: Experiential Learning I

NURS 3103.description: In this course, students learn to perform comprehensive and focused health assessments across the lifespan. They develop skills in collecting health histories, conducting physical exams, identifying priority findings, and selecting assessments based on patient needs. Students apply therapeutic communication with patients and families, use standardized tools to communicate with the healthcare team, and document findings accurately. The course emphasizes clinical reasoning, cultural awareness, patient-centered care, and professionalism in nursing practice.
NURS 3103.title: Health Assessment Across the Lifespan

NURS 3104.description: In this course, students examine the physiological and pathological mechanisms underlying common and complex health conditions across the lifespan. Students explore alterations in cellular and systemic function to understand the development and progression of disease. Emphasis is placed on connecting clinical signs and symptoms to underlying pathophysiology and understanding the rationale for medical and nursing interventions. The course fosters clinical reasoning by helping students interpret how pathophysiological processes influence patient outcomes and inform evidence-based nursing care.
NURS 3104.title: Clinical Pathophysiology for Nurses

NURS 3105.description: Students learn fundamental pharmacologic principles and their application in nursing practice. They develop the knowledge and skills needed for safe medication administration using the nursing process. Students explore evidence-based practices, dosage calculation, medication safety, and lifespan considerations. The course prepares students to manage medications responsibly and professionally across healthcare settings.
NURS 3105.title: Pharmacology For Nurses I

NURS 3106.description: Students are introduced to the foundational elements of professional identity in nursing. Students explore the values, standards, and responsibilities of the nursing profession, including ethical practice, accountability, and lifelong learning. Students explore and reflect on personal values, emotional intelligence, and self-awareness, while developing strategies to build resilience. Students develop the skills, personal strategies, and professional mindset necessary to support their success throughout the BSN program and into their nursing careers. Emphasis is placed on developing effective communication skills and professional conduct that support both personal and professional growth in nursing practice.
NURS 3106.title: Leadership Seminar I: Foundations of Professional Identity

NURS 3201.description: In this course, students build upon foundational concepts to provide nursing care for individuals with common acute and chronic conditions across the lifespan. Content includes physical and mental health conditions encountered in both community and acute care settings. Students develop age-appropriate, person-centered plans of care based on assessment findings, clinical priorities, and developmental needs. Emphasis is placed on patient safety, therapeutic communication, early recognition of changes in condition, and family-centered care. Students explore strategies for collaborating with families in caring for pediatric, adult, and older adult populations and providing individualized health education.
NURS 3201.prereqText: NURS 3101, NURS 3102, NURS 3103, NURS 3104, NURS 3105, and NURS 3106
NURS 3201.title: Nursing Care II: Common Conditions Throughout the Lifespan

NURS 3202.description: In this course, students build upon and apply foundational nursing concepts in the care of individuals with common acute and chronic conditions across the lifespan. Experiences in laboratory, simulation, community and acute care settings focus on physical and mental health care for pediatric, adult, and older adult populations. Students practice age-appropriate assessments, implement safety measures, engage in therapeutic communication, and provide person-centered, family-focused care. Emphasis is placed on clinical judgment, health education, and early recognition of changes in patient condition.
NURS 3202.prereqText: NURS 3101, NURS 3102, NURS 3103, NURS 3104, NURS 3105, and NURS 3106
NURS 3202.title: Experiential Learning II

NURS 3203.description: In this course, students explore the role of nursing scholarship, which includes research, quality improvement, and evidence-based practice, in advancing nursing care. Students examine ethical and legal considerations in research, including protection of human subjects. They also learn how to locate, critically appraise, and apply evidence from diverse sources. By comparing different approaches to nursing inquiry, students develop skills to collaborate with healthcare teams, inform clinical decisions, and propose evidence-based changes that improve patient outcomes.
NURS 3203.prereqText: NURS 3101, NURS 3102, NURS 3103, NURS 3104, NURS 3105, and NURS 3106
NURS 3203.title: Nursing Scholarship

NURS 3205.description: In this course, students expand their knowledge of pharmacology by applying core principles to the care of diverse patients across the lifespan. Students learn to evaluate medication effectiveness, recognize adverse effects and interactions, and implement safety strategies with high-alert medications. The course emphasizes advanced dosage calculations, interprofessional communication, patient education, and medication adherence support. Students strengthen clinical judgment and apply pharmacologic knowledge to promote safe, individualized nursing care.
NURS 3205.prereqText: NURS 3101, NURS 3102, NURS 3103, NURS 3104, NURS 3105, and NURS 3106
NURS 3205.title: Pharmacology for Nurses II

NURS 3206.description: In this seminar course, students explore the nurse’s role as a leader and advocate in delivering patient-centered care. Students examine and reflect on communication strategies that foster trust, empathy, and respect in diverse healthcare settings. Emphasis is placed on shared decision-making, ethical practice, and the development of patient education approaches that support informed choices and self-management. Students enhance their ability to engage patients, families, and interprofessional teams in collaborative care planning. Cultural awareness, personal values, legal frameworks, and ethical principles will be explored as integral components of effective nurse-patient relationships.
NURS 3206.prereqText: NURS 3101, NURS 3102, NURS 3103, NURS 3104, NURS 3105, and NURS 3106
NURS 3206.title: Leadership Seminar II: Patient-Centered Care

NURS 3209.description: This course is designed to introduce the student to the philosophical and theoretical basis for professional nursing across the lifespan. Emphasis is on the six processes of nursing, self-care requisites, and holistic health. Learning experiences are provided in the Nursing Learning Resource Center and diverse healthcare settings.
NURS 3209.title: Theoretical Basis for Holistic Nursing & Health

NURS 3302.description: Students analyze historical, contemporary, and global perspectives on the role of nursing in society, and on professional nursing roles within the context of contemporary health care delivery systems. Primary emphasis is on the ethical and legal foundations of nursing, including exploration of common ethical and legal dilemmas encountered at the beginning and end of life, as well as in everyday nursing encounters. In addition, students develop communication skills essential to collegial nursing practice and to collaborative roles within interdisciplinary health care teams. Students apply and critique selected models of ethical decision-making, and explore their utility for nursing practice and for assuming responsibility and accountability for nursing’s ethic of care and commitment to client advocacy.
NURS 3302.title: Professionalism and Ethics in Nursing

NURS 3303.description: An introduction to fundamental nursing pharmacologic principles and their application. The nursing process approach will be utilized in providing the theoretical base for the knowledge and skills needed to safely administer medications to patients. An in-depth review of current and evidence-based practice will be discussed when applying responsible and accountable knowledge regarding medication administration.
NURS 3303.title: Clinical Pharmacology for Nurses

NURS 3309.description: Introduction to basic interviewing and physical assessment techniques involved in the process of health assessment of clients. Emphasis is placed on recognition of normal findings, and common deviations association with pathologies.
NURS 3309.title: Health Assessment

NURS 3313.description: This course is designed to build the fundamental nursing knowledge framework and skill set necessary to safely care for adults in acute care settings using concepts of holistic nursing. Adult health nursing assists individuals and their families in promotion, maintenance, and restoration of optimal health. Learning experiences are provided in the Nursing Learning Resource Center and diverse healthcare settings.
NURS 3313.title: Adult Health Nursing

NURS 3314.description: In this course, we will apply the nursing processes to commonly encountered mental health problems across the lifespan. Note: Students in the accelerated program will have different prerequisite and concurrent prerequisite requirements. Please consult with the Assistant Director of Nursing Student Success before registration.
NURS 3314.title: Mental Health Nursing

NURS 3318.description: Application of the processes of nursing to commonly encountered problems of young adults in the childbearing years, and newborns, children, and adolescents.
NURS 3318.title: Parent-Child Nursing

NURS 3330.description: This course provides an overview of the basic structures and operations of the U.S. health system, including its major characteristics, foundations, components, finance, and future; health policy development process; and the impact of health policy on health systems and population health.
NURS 3330.title: Health Systems and Health Policy

NURS 4101.description: In this course, students learn to provide comprehensive person and family-centered care to obstetric patients and their newborns, individuals with complex physical and mental health needs, and members of special populations across the lifespan. Students expand their clinical reasoning, safety practices, and ethical decision-making. Advanced care strategies are explored, including critical thinking in clinical situations, interdisciplinary collaboration, advocacy and culturally responsive approaches to care.
NURS 4101.prereqText: NURS 3201, NURS 3202, NURS 3203, NURS 3205, and NURS 3206
NURS 4101.title: Nursing Care III: Obstetrics, Complex Conditions, and Special Populations

NURS 4102.description: In this course, students apply advanced nursing knowledge and clinical judgment to provide comprehensive person and family care to obstetric patients and their newborns, individuals with complex physical and mental health needs, and members of special populations across the lifespan. Students manage high-acuity situations, respond to complications, and coordinate care with interprofessional teams. Emphasis is placed on safe medication administration, prioritization, escalation of care, and effective communication. Students develop and implement individualized plans of care while addressing transitions, end-of-life care, and population-specific needs in both inpatient and community settings.
NURS 4102.prereqText: NURS 3201, NURS 3202, NURS 3203, NURS 3205, and NURS 3206
NURS 4102.title: Experiential Learning III

NURS 4106.description: In this seminar course, students explore the nurse’s role within healthcare systems, emphasizing systems thinking, quality improvement, and policy advocacy. Students will analyze how delivery models, regulation, and accreditation influence nursing practice and outcomes. Through interprofessional collaboration and healthcare technology, learners will evaluate and propose evidence-based strategies to improve care quality, safety, and efficiency. The course also examines cost-effectiveness and the impact of leadership in addressing system-level challenges, preparing students to drive change across diverse healthcare environments.
NURS 4106.prereqText: NURS 3201, NURS 3202, NURS 3203, NURS 3205, and NURS 3206
NURS 4106.title: Leadership Seminar III: Nursing and Systems

NURS 4201.description: In this course, students develop leadership knowledge and skills for transition to entry-level nursing practice, with an emphasis on the nurse’s role within healthcare and social systems. They synthesize knowledge from all previous nursing and supportive courses to manage evidence-based care and develop leadership skills. Students also examine population health concepts to address health disparities and improve community health. The course explores the nurse’s role as care provider, communicator, teacher, and leader.
NURS 4201.title: Nursing Care IV: Population Health and Transition to Practice

NURS 4202.description: In this course, students apply advanced nursing knowledge and leadership concepts in ambulatory and acute care settings to support the transition to professional nursing practice. Additionally, in simulated and community settings students implement principles of population health and their application in nursing practice to promote health equity and improve outcomes across diverse communities. They refine skills in communication, care coordination, and evidence-based decision-making while working with interprofessional teams.
